html:
The Pan-European Picnic was a peace event on the Austrian and Hungarian border near Sopron on 19 August 1989, during which a border gate was opened for three hours and about 600 East Germans ran through to Austria.

Hungary had begun taking down its border fence in May. Opposition groups organised the picnic with the support of Otto von Habsburg and the reform minister Imre Pozsgay, and East Germans on holiday in Hungary heard about it from leaflets. The guards did not shoot. It was the largest escape from East Germany since the Berlin Wall was built. Within weeks Hungary opened its border fully, tens of thousands left, and East Germany began to collapse, leading to the fall of the Berlin Wall in November and the wider revolutions of 1989 that ended the Cold War.
sum: The Pan-European Picnic was a peace event on the Austrian and Hungarian border near Sopron on 19 August 1989, during which a border gate was opened for three hours and about 600 East Germans ran through to Austria.
